# Scope native linker workarounds to the failing OH toolchain

## Platform difference

Native compiler/linker features that work on another target may interact differently with the selected OH SDK runtime objects and nested toolchain invocation.

## Implementation

MR changes --icf=safe to --icf=none after a reported crtn.o/SHT_LLVM_ADDRSIG incompatibility, while retaining other optimizations. NipaPlay skips a particular IPO/LTO probe in its OH CMake route because its nested toolchain invocation was reported broken.

## Applicability

These are scoped build workarounds at the referenced revisions; they are not evidence that OH forbids ICF, LTO or native optimization generally.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

Copying flags without matching the diagnostic may hide another failure or change performance/size. A probe failure and failure of the final library link are different observations.

## Verification

Reproduce the exact failing build command/toolchain, apply only the targeted workaround, inspect artifact compatibility and rerun functional/performance checks after SDK upgrades.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.

## Pinned evidence

- [NipaPlay Reload — 181bf77691](https://github.com/AimesSoft/NipaPlay-Reload/commit/181bf77691df7925b2b07cc09dc25f20fc08cd08) (diff): `ohos/entry/src/main/cpp/CMakeLists.txt`, `cpp_native/CMakeLists.txt`, `lib/plugins/js_runtime_ohos.dart`, `lib/cpp_native/native_library.dart`, `lib/src/rust/rust_external_library_io.dart`, `rust/src/api/torrent.rs`, `packages/fvp-0.37.3/ohos/src/main/ets/components/plugin/FvpPlugin.ets`, `lib/danmaku_next/next2_platform_support.dart`. Source license recorded by the study: MIT.
